                     LINK R2 OPPOSITION GROUP'S INITIAL BRIEF


       COMES NOW, Link R2 Opposition Group, hereinafter referred to as ("Link R2 Opposition

Group") and file this Brief following the Hearing on the Merits and would show the ALJ's as

follows:

                                          INTRODUCTION

           Link R2 Opposition Group has a justiciable interest in this Project because Link R2,

  fragments and would run through property owned by Link R2 Opposition Group. All members

   of Link R2 Opposition Group were admitted as intervenors to this docket.

                                          SUMMARY OF POSITION

           The primary issue in this proceeding is which route best satisfies the criteria set forth in

  the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA") and the Substantive Rules of the Public Utility

   Commission ("PUC' or "Commission"). The record shows that Route 894, or at a minimum any

  route that avoids Link R2, better satisfies the criteria because Route 894 and all routes that avoid

  Link R2 more reasonably moderate impacts on landowners,                   community values, and
  environmental resources while maintaining reasonable costs to consumers. We are opposed to

 routes 266,304, 376, 739,911, 913, and 914 ("Opposed Routes").

         Through the testimony of multiple parties, the record establishes that lower-impact

 alternatives to any route that utilizes Link R2 exist and better satisfy PURA and the

 Commission's routing criteria. Among those alternatives, Route 894 is the best-supported option

 in the record and was identified by the Applicants as the route that best meets the requirements

 ofPURA and the Commission's Substantive Rules.

       Accordingly, the Commission should select Route 894 or, at a minimum, reject any route

that utilizes Link R2.

                            Ill.    PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES

         This Initial Brief will not address the following issues from the Preliminary Order:8

  Application, Notice, Public Input, Need, Best Management Practices, Texas Parks and Wildlife

 Department, Permits, Coastal Management Program, or Limitation of Authority. This Initial Brief

  will address the Route and Cost to Consumers.

         a.      Route

         PURA § 37.056(c)(4) requires the Commission to consider several factors when

 determining whether to grant a certificate for a transmission line, including community values,

 recreational and park areas, historical and aesthetic values, and environmental integrity. The

 Commission's Substantive Rules also require that transmission lines should reasonably

 moderate impacts on affected communities and landowners while considering costs.

 Factors to consider when determining impacts on communities and landowners include whether

 the routes parallel property lines or other natural or cultural features and whether the routes

 conform with the policy of prudent avoidance, which focuses on minimizing exposure to

 electric and magnetic fields.
         Link R2 fragments many of Link IE Opposition Group's property and does not support the

  positive values identified by PURA or the Substantive Rule of the Commission, as Link R2 does not

  parallel existing property lines, roads, and/or existing utility lines. Additionally, Link R2 will affect

  the aesthetic value of the properties, and cause impacts on habitable structures are ranching

  operations. Utilizing Link R2 for the transmission line route will significantly impede the

  operation of several ranches as working ranches, recreational ranches, and hunting businesses.

  When compared to the Opposed Routes, Route 894 holistically moderates impacts on

  communities and landowners. Route 894 performs strongly on prudent avoidance, with 85

  habitable structures within 500 feet of its centerline.1 Route 487 only identified 96 habitable

  structures within 500 feet of its centerline.2 Therefore, Link R2 Opposition Group agrees with

  the Applicants and PUC Staff that Route 894 or Route 487 best meets the requirements of the

  PURA and Commission Substantive Rules for the Project. The cost to consumers

  reinforces Link R2 Opposition Group' s conclusion that Route 894 should be selected by the

  Commission.


           b. Cost to Consumers

           Route 894 is among the least expensive routes, and is one of the shortest routes at 223.2

  Miles.3 Route 894 is the Applicants' identified best-meets route and performs favorably on cost,

  with an estimated transmission line cost of $1,680,919,000 and a total estimated proj ect cost of

  $2,076,387,000.3 Specifically, the Opposed Routes inflict a higher impact that Route 894 because

  the Opposed Routes: (i) have a higher number of habitable structures within 500 feet of the

  proposed centerline ofthe right-of-way (Route 894 has only 85)4; and are longer.

           With Route 894 being one of the least expensive routes and considering the overall

           The Commission should give significant weight to the fact that either Route 894 or

  Route 487 achieves the Applicants' project objectives at a lower cost than any of Routes 266,

  304, 376, 739, 911, 913, and 9145, while simultaneously avoiding the severe impacts to the

  Link R2 Opposition Group.

           c.       Other Routes We Support/Do Not Oppose

           We also do not oppose the selection of Route 894 Western Mod. 1, 392, or 487. None of

           these Routes contain Link R2, and moderate the impacts to the Community better than the

           opposed routes.

                                              IV.      CONCLUSION


           The Opposed Routes do not reasonably balance the criteria set forth in PURA and the

  Commission's Substantive Rules when compared with Route 894. The record supports

  selecting Route 894 because it better moderates impacts on landowners, community values, and

  environmental resources while remaining reasonably cost competitive. Link R2 Opposition

  Group therefore respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges recommend Route

  894,487, or, at a minimum, reject any route that utilizes Link R2.
